title: Ignition Failure / Flame Lockout
shortDescription: The Ultra/Eco boiler failed to detect a flame after several ignition attempts and went to lockout.
fullDescription:
Weil-McLain Ultra and Eco condensing boilers display F01 when the ignition control board does not sense flame within the trial-for-ignition period. After a set number of retries the unit locks out for safety.

Common root causes include no gas supply, a closed manual gas valve, dirty or cracked ignition electrode, faulty flame-sense rod, blocked condensate trap causing combustion air imbalance, or a defective gas valve.

The boiler stays locked out until manually reset. Repeated F01 lockouts indicate a real combustion problem and need a professional combustion analyzer check.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — if you smell gas, shut off the supply, evacuate, and call your gas emergency line. Do not keep cycling reset.

causes.cause: Manual gas valve closed or LP tank empty
Air in gas line after service
Defective gas valve or ignition module

symptoms: Three audible click attempts then lockout

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Check that the manual gas shutoff at the boiler is open and other gas appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Reset the boiler
fixSteps.instruction: Press the Reset button once and watch the ignition sequence. If F01 returns, do not keep resetting.

fixSteps.title: Inspect electrode
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove the ignition electrode, clean with fine emery cloth, check the gap (typically 1/8 in).

fixSteps.title: Call a licensed tech
fixSteps.instruction: If lockout persists, have a professional verify gas pressure and combustion with an analyzer.

whenToCallPro: Any time gas pressure or combustion calibration is in question, call a licensed gas technician.

faq.q: How many times can I reset?
faq.a: Up to three resets per 15 minutes per code; if it relocks, stop and call a tech.

title: Flame Detected With Gas Valve Closed
shortDescription: The control sees a flame signal when the gas valve should be off — a safety lockout.
fullDescription:
F02 means the flame-sense circuit is reporting flame when the gas valve is commanded closed. This is treated as a stuck gas valve or shorted flame rod and the boiler locks out.

It can also occur after a wet ignition rod creates a leakage path, or when the flame-sense wire has insulation damage and is shorting to ground.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — possible stuck-open gas valve. If gas odor, shut off supply at the meter and call a professional immediately.

causes.cause: Damaged flame-sense wire shorting to ground

fixSteps.title: Cycle main power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the boiler at the service switch for 60 seconds, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect flame-sense wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafed insulation or wire pinched against metal. Replace if damaged.

fixSteps.title: Schedule a service call
fixSteps.instruction: If the code persists, have a tech check gas valve operation with a manometer.

whenToCallPro: Any suspected stuck gas valve must be diagnosed by a licensed gas technician.

faq.a: Potentially — a stuck gas valve can leak gas. Treat F02 as a real fault, not a nuisance code.

title: Blocked Air Inlet or Vent
shortDescription: The pressure switch did not close, indicating a blocked intake or flue.
fullDescription:
F03 is set when the air-pressure or vent-pressure switch fails to make on a call for heat. The boiler interprets this as restricted combustion airflow — usually a blocked flue or intake screen, but also a stuck switch.

Look for snow or ice over the termination, insect screens clogged with debris, or condensate sagging in the PVC vent run.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — a blocked flue can cause carbon monoxide spillage. Do not bypass the pressure switch.

causes.cause: Snow, ice or leaves blocking termination

symptoms: Blower runs but ignition never starts

fixSteps.title: Inspect terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Check the outdoor intake and exhaust for snow, nests, or debris. Clear gently.

fixSteps.title: Look for sagging vent
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the PVC run; any low spot will pool condensate and block the flue.

whenToCallPro: If blower or pressure switch needs replacement.

faq.q: How tall should snow clearance be?
faq.a: Keep at least 12 inches of clearance below the lowest termination — more in heavy-snow regions.

title: Low Water / LWCO Open
shortDescription: The low-water cutoff has opened or the system is below minimum pressure.
fullDescription:
F04 indicates that the LWCO probe or pressure switch is reporting insufficient water in the boiler. The Ultra/Eco hard-locks rather than firing dry.

The most common cause is a slow loss of pressure on closed-loop hydronic systems through air-vent or relief-valve weeping. Verify pressure on the gauge — typical cold-fill is 12 psi for residential.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the LWCO; firing a dry boiler can crack the heat exchanger and cause property loss.

fixSteps.title: Read pressure gauge
fixSteps.instruction: If below 12 psi cold, refill via the make-up valve to 12 psi.

fixSteps.title: Look for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check around relief valve, circulators, and visible piping for stains or moisture.

fixSteps.title: Reset boiler
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset; if pressure holds and flame establishes you are done.

whenToCallPro: If pressure will not hold or LWCO probe needs replacing.

faq.q: How often should I top up?
faq.a: A sealed system should rarely need top-ups; frequent refills point to a leak.

title: Supply Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The boiler supply (outlet) temperature sensor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription:
The supply sensor (S5/S6) provides modulation feedback. F05 trips when the resistance is outside the expected NTC curve. Often a connector backed out during service or a sensor that has corroded at the well.

The boiler will not run with a missing supply sensor as it cannot protect the heat exchanger from over-temperature.
safetyWarning: Power off the service switch before disconnecting any sensor leads.

causes.cause: Loose sensor connector at the board

fixSteps.title: Reseat the connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, unplug and replug the supply sensor connector at the control.

fixSteps.title: Ohm the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: At room temperature an NTC10K reads ~10 kΩ. Replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: If the sensor well is part of the heat exchanger and requires draining the boiler.

faq.a: Use the OEM Weil-McLain part — third-party NTCs can have a different beta value.

title: Return Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Return-water temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription: F06 covers the return NTC. This sensor lets the control compute delta-T and protect against thermal shock. A failure may simply disable modulation or hard-lock the unit depending on firmware revision.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power before working on sensors.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the return sensor pigtail is seated firmly at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Drain to below the well, swap the NTC, refill and bleed.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable draining and refilling a hydronic loop.

faq.q: Will the boiler run without it?
faq.a: Some firmware allows reduced-rate operation; most Eco units lock out.

title: Combustion Blower Fault
shortDescription: The combustion blower is not reaching commanded RPM feedback.
fullDescription:
F09 is logged when the variable-speed combustion fan does not match the tach feedback that the control expects, or fails to start at all. The fault commonly follows a debris ingestion event, a bad fan PWM cable, or an aged fan motor.

Until the blower spins up correctly the boiler will not attempt ignition.
safetyWarning: Live AC at the blower terminals — disconnect power before opening the fan housing.
symptoms: No fan sound on call for heat

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan inlet
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove inlet adapter, clear any debris from the impeller.

fixSteps.title: Verify connections
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the 4-pin PWM cable on the fan and at the control.

fixSteps.title: Replace blower
fixSteps.instruction: If the fan is dead or seized, replace the assembly with the OEM part.

whenToCallPro: If the blower is failed or combustion needs to be re-set with an analyzer.

faq.q: Can I run without the fan?
faq.a: No — the boiler is fully sealed-combustion; the fan is mandatory.

title: Flue/Stack Over-Temperature
shortDescription: Flue temperature exceeded the safe limit.
fullDescription: F13 means the flue thermistor saw above-limit temperature, typically over 200 °F on a condensing unit. Over-temp is usually caused by a heat-exchanger fouled with combustion deposits or by high firing rate against a closed-loop system that is not absorbing heat (deadheaded pump, closed zone valves).
safetyWarning: Repeated flue over-temp can damage PVC vent material — do not bypass the limit.

causes.cause: Failed circulator or stuck zone valve

symptoms: F13 on display after a long run

fixSteps.title: Verify flow
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the system circulator is running and at least one zone is open during the call.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a technician open and brush-clean the heat exchanger.

whenToCallPro: Heat-exchanger cleaning and combustion analysis are pro-only.

faq.q: How often should the HX be cleaned?
faq.a: Annual service is recommended for Weil-McLain Eco/Ultra condensing units.

title: High Limit Trip
shortDescription: Supply temperature exceeded the high-limit threshold and the boiler locked out.
fullDescription:
E01 indicates the supply or stack high-limit opened. Causes include rapid temperature spike from low flow, air in the heat exchanger, or a failed circulator.

Reset will succeed once temperature falls below the differential, but recurrence means an underlying flow problem.
safetyWarning: Do not jumper out the high limit; loss of this protection can scald and damage the system.

fixSteps.title: Bleed the boiler
fixSteps.instruction: Use the air vent at the supply to purge trapped air.

fixSteps.title: Verify circulator
fixSteps.instruction: Place a hand on the pump; vibration should be felt during a call. Replace if dead.

whenToCallPro: If circulator replacement or system rebalancing is needed.

faq.q: Why does it happen only on cold mornings?
faq.a: Long off-cycles let air come out of solution; a fresh bleed usually solves it.

title: Internal Control Fault
shortDescription: The boiler control reports an internal/self-test failure.
fullDescription:
E02 is a self-diagnostic failure on the ignition control. The board failed an internal RAM/relay self-check on power-up. A surge event, water intrusion in the cabinet, or a long-life failure of the board are typical causes.

A single occurrence may clear with a power cycle; recurring E02 means board replacement.
safetyWarning: Disconnect line power at the breaker before opening the cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the breaker off for two minutes, then back on.

fixSteps.title: Schedule replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If E02 returns, the control board needs to be replaced by a tech.

whenToCallPro: Board replacement requires gas valve commissioning afterward.

faq.q: Should I add a surge protector?
faq.a: Yes — a whole-house or boiler-circuit surge device prolongs control life.

title: Inducer Fan Speed Out of Range
shortDescription: Combustion fan RPM is outside operating window.
fullDescription: Weil-McLain Ultra Eco fault F07 indicates the inducer fan tachometer is reporting RPM outside the commanded window. Common causes include dust accumulation, bearing wear, or PCB driver issues.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; vacuum the inducer fan blades.

title: Flame Loss During Operation
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F08 reports that flame was established but then lost during run. Causes include weak gas pressure, contaminated flame rod, or vent recirculation.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Gas pressure verification by technician if cleaning fails.

faq.a: Brief flame loss is contained but persistent loss should be addressed.

title: Supply Sensor Out of Range
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F10 indicates the supply temperature sensor is open or shorted. The boiler cannot regulate output without it and locks out for safety.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the supply sensor connector.

title: Return Sensor Out of Range
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F11 indicates the return-water sensor is failed. Used for outdoor reset and condensing efficiency calculations.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

faq.a: Some models lock out; others run with reduced features.

title: Outdoor Sensor Out of Range
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F12 indicates the outdoor air sensor is open or shorted. Outdoor reset is unavailable; boiler defaults to fixed setpoint.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Check the outdoor sensor wire for damage.

title: DHW Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: Indirect domestic hot water sensor failed.
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F14 indicates the indirect water heater tank sensor is failed. DHW priority is unavailable.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement requires access to the indirect tank.

title: Condensate Trap Blocked
shortDescription: Excessive backpressure in the condensate trap.
fullDescription: Weil-McLain F15 indicates the condensate trap is restricted, possibly clogged with biological growth or sludge. Cleaning is straightforward.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Clean Trap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the condensate trap.

whenToCallPro: Persistent issues may indicate vent / drain plumbing problems.

title: Reset Limit Exceeded
shortDescription: User has exceeded the maximum manual reset count.
fullDescription: Weil-McLain E03 indicates the boiler has been reset too many times in a short period. Investigate the underlying fault rather than resetting.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Wait Lockout Period
fixSteps.instruction: Allow the lockout timer to expire (typically 1 hour).

whenToCallPro: Investigate prior fault codes — call a technician.

faq.a: No — the lockout is a safety feature.

title: Boiler Overheat
fullDescription: Weil-McLain E04 indicates the manual reset hi-limit has tripped due to overheat. After cooling, manually reset and investigate cause.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Manual Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press the manual reset button on the hi-limit.

whenToCallPro: Investigate root cause — pump or zone valve replacement may be needed.

faq.a: Single events usually OK; repeated events damage the heat exchanger.

title: Rollout Switch Open
fullDescription: Weil-McLain E05 indicates the flame rollout switch has opened, signaling flame escaped the combustion chamber. This is a serious safety event requiring technician inspection.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Do not reset and run — call a technician immediately.

faq.q: Should I run if it clears?
